title: A larger star at equal temperature
hook: Change stellar radius and predict ideal blackbody luminosity.
misconception: ideal blackbody luminosity doubles when stellar radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply L = 4πR²σT⁴ to compare ideal blackbody luminosity when stellar radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a spherical blackbody with fixed absolute surface temperature, L = 4πR²σT⁴. When stellar radius doubles, ideal blackbody luminosity becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model L = 4πR²σT⁴; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a spherical blackbody with fixed absolute surface temperature, with a nonzero initial result. If stellar radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on ideal blackbody luminosity?
recall.why: Apply L = 4πR²σT⁴ under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
